purpose: Paired diagnostic interventions on CPU scheduling period and external CPU contention; no refit or validation of a boundary model.
execution: Four fresh-stack conditions sequentially on each hosted runner, with each condition occupying each ordinal position once. All directed adjacent condition pairs occur once. Load starts only after limits and health checks; each stack has fresh volumes. The idle/busy auxiliary container has the same pinned image and 0.5-CPU ceiling in both conditions; only its shell command changes.
background_scope: External contention, not a donor or receiver within the unchanged 3.4-CPU SUT budget. One shell busy loop can consume at most 0.5 CPU; actual delivered consumption must be reported, not assumed.
measurement: Reuse the frozen 40/s checkout and 100/s advertising workloads, fixed VUs, timeout/censoring rules and externally measured SLO. Store every request and all windows. Sample all running containers, host CPU components and pressure, cgroup CPU/memory/pressure and auxiliary-container activity.
analysis: Independently rescore raw primary events. Pool the two post-warmup start cohorts for a session p95, retaining both separate windows. Per runner, report short-minus-long at both background levels, busy-minus-idle at both periods and their interaction. Report errors and actual CPU/throttling alongside latency. Censored p95 values are lower bounds, never exact contrast estimates. Four runner blocks, not eight windows per condition, are independent units. No success threshold or significance claim.
validity: Check configured and actual period/quota integers and RAM/swap limits before and after measurement; sample actual cpu.max throughout. Missing primary evidence, generator failure, lost telemetry or changed limits prevent a complete diagnostic block, but all recoverable outcomes remain visible. SUT restarts/OOM are diagnostics, not exclusions or forced SLO labels. Dropped operations remain failures and separately invalidate offered-load matching. No outcome-driven retries; rerun only infrastructure failures, retaining attempts and selecting the latest whole block.
